lines.text: Deep in the Andes lies a lake of legend, and a king coated head to toe in gold — El Dorado, the dream that drove the world mad. Colombia, land of the golden men, plays like it too.
But out of West Africa march the Black Stars — proud, powerful, a shining light on the flag of a continent. Tonight, the golden king meets the black star.
Welcome back to WorldCup twenty-six Legends — episode ninety-two. Colombia, versus Ghana. A knockout. Win, or the dream dies right here.
Colombia arrive as the Cafeteros — samba in their feet, gold on their backs, and two of the game's great artists. Ghana arrive as the Black Stars — four-time kings of Africa, fearless and physical.
Colombia — Los Cafeteros. Golden, joyful, and blessed with pure magic.

James Rodríguez, the captain, still paints passes no one else can even see. Luis Díaz is the lightning down the left, electric and fearless. And Jhon Durán is the young cannon who shoots from anywhere.
Richard Ríos drives the engine with power and poise. And Dávinson Sánchez is the tower that guards the gold.
Ghana — the Black Stars. Kings of Africa, fast, fearless, and hungry.
Jordan Ayew, the captain, leads the line with a warrior's heart. Mohammed Kudus is the jewel, a dribble like silk and a shot like thunder. And Thomas Partey runs the midfield like a metronome.
Iñaki Williams burns the channels with frightening pace. And Mohammed Salisu is the wall that will not break.
So here is the riddle. Does the golden king shine too bright for the stars? Or do the Black Stars steal the gold?
And stay with me — because this one turns, late, on a flash of pure lightning.
Here is how we see it. Ghana come out flying, powerful and fearless, and the golden men are rocked back on their heels.
The Black Stars strike first. All of Colombia holds its breath.
And it lands. Ghana score, and the Black Stars lead. The stars are shining now.
But gold does not tarnish. Colombia steady, the ball finds James, and the artist goes to work.
And James Rodríguez levels it — one-one. A touch of pure gold.
And then, late, the lightning. Luis Díaz strikes, and Colombia lead. Two — one. The golden king stands.
Two — one. Ghana were brilliant, and brave, and so nearly there — but the gold of Colombia shone through in the end.
Our prediction — Colombia two, Ghana one. Díaz, late. Not played yet — the real ninety is yours to watch.
And Ghana leave with their heads high — the Black Stars who made the golden men sweat for every inch.
Colombia march on. El Dorado, still shining, still lighting up the tournament in gold.
So you tell me — the golden king, or the black star? Comment COLOMBIA for the Cafeteros — comment GHANA for the Black Stars.
For five hundred years they hunted it — the king of gold, the lake of legend, the dream no conqueror could ever hold. Legend ninety-two — El Dorado, the Golden King.
The players write the night. But El Dorado carries one truth — real gold is not taken, it is earned. And it shines brightest under pressure.
